summary: `execFileWithShimRetry`'s shell retry re-parses the argv it is handed with nothing bounding it, and `shellArgs` puts a consumer's whole command line there as one word
acceptance: the win32 shim retry refuses an argv word a shell re-parse would rewrite — naming the word, with the spawn failure as `cause` — so a consumer's declared command line reaches the shim intact or says why it cannot; the retry over an argv every word of which survives is unchanged, and the predicate has one home the provider's own mechanics read too
tests: execFileWithShimRetry refuses the win32 shim retry when an argv word would not survive the shell's re-parse
notes: Off note THE-SHIM-RETRY-ARGV-SURVIVES-ITS-OWN-SHELL item 1, re-verified: the note read the exposure as latent, it is not. `shellArgs` (`harness/declaredShell.ts:32`) is `["-c", line]` and reaches the retry at `src/builtinGates.ts:74` (via `harness/declaredGates.ts:165`) and `harness/chain.ts:588`. `src/builtinGates.ts:70` declares a flags-only tradeoff those callers do not meet. `claudeCode`'s `budgetArgs.length > 0` branch (`src/claudeCode.ts:204`) is the instance this generalizes.
